Added the geometric-mean variant to the descriptive-stats reference. This captures two generalizable things future runs will benefit from:

1. **Geometric mean convention** — use exp(mean(log(x))) / nth-root-of-product, NOT arithmetic mean. The two are deceptively close for clustered rates, so an arithmetic slip can still look plausible but miss the rounded thousandth.

2. **Weekly Treasury-bill auction rate table** — a distinct table (money-market / new-bill-issues section, keyed by issue date) from the monthly outlays/yields tables already documented. Plus the pooling rule (collect every weekly issue in the named month across all named years into one list; don't average per-year first) and the 91-day-vs-182-day series distinction.

I didn't touch SKILL.md (it's >100KB so patching is blocked, and the existing pointer to descriptive-stats-over-months.md already routes here). No memory update needed — the durable facts (delimiter modes, table conventions) are already recorded and this is a statistic/table-specific procedure that belongs in the reference, not memory.

Skill updated, not "no skill needed" — this was a genuinely new statistic + table combination.
